intro.data: Identity works on the far side too. Your tray holds the Parser and two B→B steps: one keeps the clean table, the other smudges it. Bring the Parser and the real do-nothing step onto the board and wire them, leaving the smudger in the tray.
intro.alchemy: Identity works on the far side too. Your tray holds the Smelter and two B→B steps: one keeps the ingot, the other taints it. Bring the Smelter and the real do-nothing step onto the board and wire them, leaving the tainter in the tray.
intro.spellcraft: Identity works on the far side too. Your tray holds Ignition and two B→B steps: one keeps the flame, the other warps it. Bring Ignition and the real do-nothing step onto the board and wire them, leaving the warper in the tray.
intro.abstract: id works after f too. Here the values are plain numbers: f sends 4 ↦ 12, the identity returns its number unchanged (12 ↦ 12), and the look-alike alters it (12 ↦ 15). Bring f and the true identity from the tray onto the board and wire them, leaving the look-alike behind.

goal.data: Bring the Parser and a real do-nothing step from the tray and wire them, ending at the clean table.
goal.alchemy: Bring the Smelter and a real do-nothing step from the tray and wire them, ending at the ingot.
goal.spellcraft: Bring Ignition and a real do-nothing step from the tray and wire them, ending at the flame.
goal.abstract: Bring f and id_B from the tray and wire them so the input reaches the goal value, leaving the look-alike in the tray.

afterSuccess.data: The do-nothing step after the Parser kept the clean table exactly as it was. The Smudger was the same type but changed it. id_B ∘ f = f — identity is neutral on either side.
afterSuccess.alchemy: The do-nothing step after the Smelter kept the ingot exactly as it was. id_B ∘ f = f — identity is neutral on either side.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: The do-nothing step after Ignition kept the flame exactly as it was. id_B ∘ f = f — identity is neutral on either side.
afterSuccess.abstract: Identity after f left the result unchanged: id_B ∘ f = f. The look-alike altered it.

reveal.summary: Identity morphisms are two-sided units: id_B ∘ f = f and f ∘ id_A = f, for the genuine identity that leaves every value alone.
reveal.moreFormal: Whether before or after, the identity contributes nothing to a composite — provided it truly is the do-nothing map.
